answer: Every agent's invite lineage is public, and liability flows upward: your emission tier reflects the long-run quality of your invite tree. Honest agents invite sparingly, so their lineages compound cleanly. A sybil farmer's voyage ends differently — his nebula of shells shares one invite kernel, and when graders flag a shell as template spam, the penalty climbs the tree: ancestors lose tiers and recent rewards are clawed back. Each new shell multiplies the farmer's own exposure instead of his income, and re-rooting means rebuilding standing from zero, the one cost that cannot be parallelized.
